title: Provide assistance in implementing and assuring project work is conducted in accordance with the project quality plan

lessons.title: Understanding the project quality plan
lessons.html:
Understanding the project quality plan

A project is a piece of work with a clear goal, a start and an end date and a budget. At a grain silo or farm, projects include building a new bin, installing a grain dryer, replacing a conveyor, upgrading the weighbridge or refurbishing a bunker. A project quality plan is the document that says what quality the project must deliver and how the team will make sure it does.

What a quality plan usually contains

  • Scope and quality requirements: what must be delivered and the standards it must meet, for example the drawings, specifications, manufacturer's installation instructions and applicable SANS standards named by the engineer.
  • Roles and responsibilities: who is the project manager, who checks quality, who signs off each stage.
  • Inspection and test plan (ITP): a list of checks, when they happen, what the acceptance limit is, and who witnesses them. Some are hold points: work may not continue until the check is signed.
  • Procedures: how to handle materials, how to calibrate measuring tools, how to record results.
  • Non-conformance procedure: what to do when something does not meet requirements.
  • Records: which forms, checklists and photos must be kept.

Your role in assisting

At NQF level 3 you support the project manager or quality controller. You help make sure the team knows the plan and follows it on site. That means:

  1. Reading the parts of the plan that apply to your team's work.
  2. Explaining the checks and hold points to workers before a task starts.
  3. Making sure the right version of drawings and checklists is on site.
  4. Checking that measuring tools, such as tape measures, levels and torque wrenches, are in calibration.
  5. Raising questions early when the plan is unclear.

Quality is cheaper when it is built in from the start. A foundation poured in the wrong place, or a conveyor bolted with the wrong grade bolts, costs far more to fix later than it would have cost to check first.

lessons.title: Checking work, recording and handling non-conformance
lessons.html:
Checking work and handling non-conformance

Carrying out checks

Follow the inspection and test plan. For each check:

  1. Know the requirement: the dimension, tolerance, material grade or test result needed.
  2. Use the right, calibrated tool.
  3. Check at the right time. Some checks are only possible before the next layer covers the work, for example reinforcing steel before concrete is poured.
  4. Record the result on the checklist, with date, location and your signature. Add a photo if the plan asks for it.
  5. At a hold point, stop the work and call the person who must sign it off.

Example

A contractor is erecting a new steel silo. The ITP says the base ring must be level within the limit on the drawing before the next ring is fitted. You check with a level at several points, find one side out, and record it. The work stops until the base is shimmed and rechecked. The fix takes an hour. Finding it after ten rings were up would have cost days.

Non-conformance

A non-conformance is any work, material or process that does not meet the requirement. When you find one:

  • Stop the affected work if continuing would make it worse or unsafe.
  • Mark or tag the item so it is not used by mistake.
  • Report it to the quality controller or project manager straight away, using the non-conformance report (NCR) form.
  • Describe it with facts: what, where, when, what the requirement was and what was found.
  • Do not fix it in your own way without approval. The fix (rework, repair, accept as is, or reject) is decided by the responsible person.
  • After the fix, recheck and record that it is closed.

Keeping records

Quality records prove the work was done right. File them in the project file in order. Keep them clean and readable. They are needed for hand-over to the client and for any future claim or repair.

Key points

  • The project quality plan sets the requirements, checks, responsibilities and records.
  • Brief the team on checks and hold points before work starts.
  • Use calibrated tools and check at the right stage.
  • Report non-conformances with facts on an NCR and do not fix them without approval.
  • Keep complete, readable quality records.

quiz.question: What is a hold point in an inspection and test plan?

options.text: A tea break for the team
A check that must be signed off before work may continue
A place where materials are stored
The end date of the project

quiz.question: Why should reinforcing steel be checked before concrete is poured?

options.text: Because it cannot be checked once it is covered
Because the client asks for it

quiz.question: You find a non-conformance. What should you NOT do?

options.text: Fix it your own way without approval

quiz.question: What is your main role when assisting with the quality plan at this level?

options.text: Making sure the team knows the plan and follows it on site

quiz.question: Which is a good description on a non-conformance report?

options.text: Base ring out of level on the east side, beyond the drawing limit, found at 10:00 on 3 May
